lines: - Speed up the parse phase without changing the emitted issues: no `ParseVisitor` is created for nodes of the 88 kinds whose handler only returns the current context (most nodes; a unit test checks the list against the handlers of `ParseVisitor`), the AST simplifier no longer checks the elements of an array literal for side effects when none of them would be trimmed and no longer creates an array per node it visits, doc comments without a multi-line annotation skip the multi-line reduction, finding the line of a `@param`/`@return` tag splits the file with `explode()` instead of `preg_split()` (the doc comment lines contain no newlines, so the comparisons are the same) and reuses the absolute path of the file, types without template parameters no longer create a closure, and the check that a file to parse still exists uses `file_exists()` instead of `realpath()`. This makes the parse phase about 12 % faster on a large project.

- Skip the checks that only emit issues about the declaration of a function or method (the order of `@param` tags, promotion modifiers, required parameters after optional ones, impossible types without intersection types, default values, `@override`/`@inheritDoc` comments) when it is declared in a file excluded from analysis, such as `vendor/`, including the methods that classes inherit from those files. Phan discarded those issues anyway. The steps that the rest of the analysis depends on still run: scope initialization, phpdoc type narrowing and inheritance, return type inference, inherited `@throws` types, attributes, duplicate definition checks, the plugins' `analyzeFunction`/`analyzeMethod`, the signature compatibility checks against overridden methods and the impossible-combination checks of intersection types (both expand types, which hydrates classes), and the lookups of the classes used in parameter, return and `@throws` types, which load internal classes (for parameter and return types of these elements, they now run once per type instead of once per function or method). This makes the method analysis phase about 8 % faster on a large project where most methods are declared in excluded files, without changing the issues reported. Set `PHAN_ANALYZE_EXCLUDED_METHODS=1` to run the checks anyway. `PHAN_VERIFY_SKIPPED_CHECKS=1` runs them and exits with an error if any of them emitted an issue in an analyzed file, modified the function or method, or threw. `PHAN_DUMP_METHOD_STATE_DIGEST=<path>` writes the types and flags of every user-defined function and method and the order in which internal methods were loaded when the analysis phase starts, to compare runs with and without `PHAN_ANALYZE_EXCLUDED_METHODS=1`.

- Skip two walks over the methods that an inherited method overrides when they cannot find anything, without changing the emitted issues: the search for an inherited `@phan-mandatory-param` when no method with the same name has a parameter marked `@phan-mandatory-param`, and the search for inherited `@throws` types when no method with the same name declares `@throws`. This is never done for `__construct` (default constructors are created lazily), and not at all once a class was hydrated while the hydration of one of its ancestors was unfinished (e.g. an inheritance cycle). `PHAN_VERIFY_SKIPPED_CHECKS=1` also runs these walks and exits with an error if one of them found something, initialized the scope of a user-defined method, hydrated a class or threw, or if the overridden methods of a method whose walks were skipped changed by the end of the method analysis phase. Also, the checks for references to classes that are declared more than once no longer look up a second declaration of classes declared once, and finding the parameters that take callables or class names (for the internal callable checks and `AnalyzeCallableArgumentCapability` plugins) no longer allocates two closures per parameter. On a large project with about 640,000 inherited methods, this makes the method analysis phase about 5 % faster (18.7 s -> 17.8 s), the plugin loading step about 15 % faster and the whole run about 2 % faster at `-j 1`.

+- Replay the declaration analysis of inherited methods instead of repeating it, without changing the emitted issues. Phan creates the methods that a class inherits as copies of the methods of its ancestors before analyzing them, and analyzes each method before its copies. The part of that analysis that only depends on the declaration (adding phpdoc and default value types to the parameters, the phpdoc parameter types, `@phan-mandatory-param`, narrowing parameter types to their phpdoc types and the checks of the parameters) now records what it read from a method and what it wrote to it, if it checked no issue (not even a suppressed one) and found no template type. For a copy that has the same inputs (the same comment, context, flags, real parameters, and parameter types, flags and defaults), Phan writes the recorded results instead of computing them again: the same computation from the same inputs would produce the same results and check no issue either, and every class it hydrated or internal class it loaded already was. Everything else still runs for each copy (the checks against the methods it overrides, attributes, return types, `@throws`, plugins). This is never done for `__construct`, for methods of classes declared more than once, when an inherited `@phan-mandatory-param` has to be looked up, or when only some files are analyzed (daemon mode). Set `PHAN_DISABLE_CLONE_REPLAY=1` to analyze every copy. `PHAN_VERIFY_SKIPPED_CHECKS=1` analyzes the copies that would be replayed and exits with an error if their analysis checked an issue, hydrated a class, loaded an internal class or added a method, or produced different results; it now also runs the class lookups of parameter and return types that are skipped for elements declared in excluded files inside the same verification as the other skipped checks. On a large project with about 640,000 inherited methods, 89 % of those that are copies of another method are replayed, which makes the method analysis phase about 20 % faster (17.5 s -> 14.0 s), the whole run about 6 % faster at `-j 1` and `-j 4`, and peak memory about 2.5 % lower (the copies share the type objects of their source).

- Analysis workers of `--processes N` now terminate without running PHP's shutdown sequence once they have sent their results to the parent (by exec'ing `/bin/true`). Destroying the inherited heap wrote to every object, which copied the copy-on-write pages shared with the parent and the other workers (several GB per worker on large projects) and delayed the parent's output by seconds. Set `PHAN_DISABLE_FAST_EXIT=1` to keep the regular `exit()`; it is also kept when the profiler, xdebug or pcov is active. Analysis results are unchanged.

+ * Replays the declaration analysis of inherited methods in Analysis::analyzeFunctions().
+ * Clazz::addMethod() creates the methods that a class inherits as clones of the methods of its ancestors,
+ * and records the method each one was cloned from (its source) in the clone. Analysis::analyzeFunctions()
+ * processes each source before its clones. The "declaration analysis" of a method is the part of that processing
+ * which only depends on the method's own declaration: the parameters part of ensureScopeInitialized()
+ * (phpdoc and default types of the parameters, the phpdoc parameter type map, (at)phan-mandatory-param offsets,
+ * whether it has template types) and ParameterTypesAnalyzer::analyzeParameterTypesOfDeclaration()
+ * (narrowing the parameter types to the phpdoc types, and the checks of the parameters).
+ * For a source, this records everything that its declaration analysis reads from the method before it
+ * (Method::getCloneReplayFingerprint()) and everything that it writes after it (Method::getCloneReplaySnapshot()),
+ * if it neither checked nor emitted an issue (Issue::$emit_attempt_count), and found no template type.
+ * When a clone of it has the same fingerprint, its declaration analysis would compute the same results from the same
+ * inputs and check no issue either, so Analysis::analyzeFunctions() replays the snapshot instead of running it
+ * (Method::replayDeclarationAnalysis()), and runs all other steps (signature checks against the methods it overrides,
+ * attributes, return types, (at)throws, plugins) as before. The declaration analysis also reads state outside of the method:
+ * - The configuration, and the existence of classes (fixed once parsing is done).
+ * - Classes are hydrated and internal classes are loaded the first time they are needed. The source's identical
+ *   declaration analysis already did that, so the clone's would do nothing more.
+ * - EmitOnlyChecks::modeForClassLookup(): its result only depends on which types were already looked up,
+ *   and the source's declaration analysis looked up the same types.
+ * - The walk over the methods that the method overrides for an inherited (at)phan-mandatory-param:
+ *   this only replays clones for which that walk is skipped (see EmitOnlyChecks::beginAnalyzingMethod()).
+ * A replayed clone that other methods were cloned from gets the record of its source, since it has the same state.
+ * (The source is only used to find a record: the fingerprint alone decides whether replaying it is identical.)
+ * With PHAN_VERIFY_SKIPPED_CHECKS=1, the declaration analysis of the clones that could be replayed runs instead,
+ * and this verifies that it checked or emitted no issue, had no side effects other than initializing the scope,
+ * and produced the state that the replay would have produced. Then it sets the state of the clone to the objects
+ * of the snapshot (instead of the equal objects that the declaration analysis created), so that the following
+ * decisions (which compare objects by identity) are the same as without PHAN_VERIFY_SKIPPED_CHECKS=1.
+ * This is not part of Phan's plugin API.
